A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. Their main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable matching despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v2 reports original synthetic experiments in Figures 1–3 and evaluations of the proposed methods on PetShop in Appendix C.4.

after.justification: v3 reports original synthetic experiments, graph-misspecification tests, and PetShop, Sock-shop and ProRCA evaluations in Section 4 and Appendix F.

M1.justification: TOCA, proposed in v2 Section 3 and Appendix A, is removed. The existing SCORE ORDERING heuristic becomes a confidence-based shortlist procedure using an in-degree bound and a stopping criterion in v3 Algorithm 2. SMOOTH TRAVERSAL retains its basic largest-parent-score-gap rule.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained synthetic and PetShop evaluations, v3 adds Sock-shop data covering 125 injected microservice faults and ProRCA retail-service simulations covering four anomaly types. It also evaluates scenarios with incorrect causal graphs.

E2.justification: Cholesky is added to the retained synthetic and PetShop comparisons, introducing a direct competitor that also operates without the causal graph. Synthetic extensions additionally evaluate RCD and epsilon-Diagnosis, which appeared only in the PetShop comparisons in v2. TOCA comparison curves disappear.

E3.justification: The core synthetic setup retains 1,000 normal observations and 100 repetitions. New protocols include exclusively linear models, polytree constraints, and controlled edge additions, removals and reversals. Additional comparisons give RCD and epsilon-Diagnosis 100 anomalous samples synthetically and 361 on Sock-shop, versus one for the other methods.

E4.justification: v3 tests whether linearity explains baseline performance, whether polytree restrictions affect performance, and how graph misspecification degrades recall (Appendices F.2 and F.4). Table 3 newly quantifies PetShop score ties. The earlier anomaly-strength, graph-size and random-tie analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v3 introduces explicit error bars on recall in Figure 8, whereas v2's recall curves lack them. The retained synthetic sweeps still report 100 repetitions. The later PDF does not explain the bars' calculation or identify them as standard errors, standard deviations or confidence intervals.

E6.justification: Shared PetShop scores are retained, but Cholesky adds new comparisons: its temporal-latency top-1 recall after random tie-breaking is 0.50 versus SCORE ORDERING's 0.10 (v3 Table 4). Synthetic curves are revised, TOCA results disappear, and substantial robustness and benchmark results are added. ProRCA SMOOTH TRAVERSAL recalls range from 0.04 to 0.28 (Table 10).

T1.justification: v3 replaces the TOCA/dominating-root-cause and chain-specific development with score-typicality and polytree analysis, while retaining contribution lemmas in Appendices A/C. It adds joint-parent scores, maximum-gap and top-k bounds (Theorems 3.12–3.13), marginal-score sample complexity (Appendix B), and beyond-polytree analysis (Appendix E). Equation 5 also changes to include the scored observation.

C1.justification: v3 withdraws TOCA as a headline contribution and explicitly qualifies the principal marginal-score guarantees by the polytree setting. It introduces probabilistic correctness and shortlist guarantees for the two retained methods. The conclusion additionally claims uniquely general nonparametric guarantees for RCA from a single anomalous sample.

C2.justification: v3 adds substantive discussion of applicability beyond polytrees, linearity-dependent baseline performance, and Sock-shop/ProRCA failures. It retains and quantifies the PetShop tie limitation and cautions against comparisons with unequal sample availability. One new interpretation is overstated: F.7 suggests epsilon-Diagnosis improves memory-fault detection, although Tables 6–9 report 0.00 memory recall.

D1.justification: v3 supplies a reproduction-code address absent from v2 and documents baseline implementation sources, default settings, Traversal's threshold of 3, and Cholesky variant choices. It adds graph-perturbation and benchmark-processing instructions. The detailed synthetic generator and Apple M1/16 GB hardware disclosure are retained.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning against Li et al.'s Cholesky approach, including its implications for score-ordering counterexamples. New references cover polytrees, conformal outlier testing, outlier propagation and additional benchmarks. The core counterfactual and traversal lineage remains, while several references associated with removed discussions disappear.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, preliminaries and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The narrative now begins with causal Bayesian networks; retained counterfactual contribution analysis moves to Appendix A. Theory and experiments are reorganized, new explanatory examples are introduced, and a publication checklist is added.

P2.justification: v3 adds a polytree schematic, algorithm boxes for the retained methods, diagnostic plots and additional benchmark tables. Existing plots have revised legends and displays; PetShop tables gain Cholesky columns and are rearranged. The document adopts conference formatting with substantially revised figure and table placement.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a substantially more informative evaluation: it tests v2's conjecture about linearity, adds graph-error controls and a relevant graph-free competitor, and exposes failures on Sock-shop and ProRCA. Explicit polytree qualifications, additional formal analysis and reproduction information make the retained methods' strengths and limits easier to assess. TOCA's removal narrows scope; undefined error bars and the F.7 memory-fault overstatement are shortcomings, but they do not outweigh these substantial gains.
